- After all that and the $6,000 trip, you'd be **$1,932.53 short**. That's before any eating out, shopping, entertainment or health spending.

That still leaves roughly $830 uncovered, which would have to come out of your $20,000 savings goal or your Roth contribution. Both are top priorities for you.

A smaller trip could work. Your discretionary spending is a few hundred dollars a month, so aim for something in the low thousands, or wait for next month's income. Treat that as a rough estimate until you've checked what you've already spent this month.
